definition: Artificial intelligence (AI) has many applications in warfare, including in communications, intelligence, and munitions control.
details: AI is not limited to new weapons such as drones or strategic means such as cyberwar, as it can affect all forms of military planning.

explainer.lead: Artificial intelligence has many applications in warfare, including in communications, intelligence, and munitions control. It matters because AI is not confined to new weapons like drones or strategic means like cyberwar — it can affect all forms of military planning.

tiers.eli5: Armies use computers for many jobs beyond robot weapons — like handling messages, sorting information, and deciding where to aim — and this touch every kind of planning.
tiers.practitioner: Those working on defence systems must treat AI as spanning communications, intelligence and munitions control rather than as a single weapons category. A pitfall is assuming only novel platforms such as drones or cyberwar matter, when AI can affect all forms of military planning.
tiers.paperLevel: The definition states that AI has applications in warfare including communications, intelligence, and munitions control, and that it can affect all forms of military planning, not only new weapons such as drones or strategic means such as cyberwar.

explainer.example: An intelligence unit using AI to sift communications is an application of AI in warfare under this definition, just as a drone's targeting system is.
